Grade: PP1

Strand: MEASUREMENT 3.2 Mass By the end of the sub- • Demonstrate lifting objects of 1. 
Topic 3.3: Capacity (how

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Capacity (how. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: how many small how many small ones seeds or sand ones fill the big ones and vice versa can be filled?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Use Capacity (how to solve everyday problems

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Capacity (how.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Capacity (how using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In groups or pairs, individually, learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size.
2. Watch a video on filling and emptying containers.
3. Environmental activities as they play filling and emptying.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how many small how many small ones seeds or sand ones fill the big ones and vice versa can be filled?
2. Which container holds containers using water, and small containers by telling how many more or less?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Capacity (how is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
